concept.name: Outcome metric
concept.definition: A measure of trading results - net P&L, expectancy, win rate, average R-multiple, drawdown, risk-adjusted return - capturing what the strategy earned rather than how it was executed. Outcome metrics are the ultimate test of a process but are noisy and must not be read trade by trade.
concept.intuition: Outcomes are the scoreboard, but over any small number of games the scoreboard mostly measures luck.
concept.mechanics: Computed from closed trades: expectancy combines win rate with average win and loss sizes; R-distributions, maximum drawdown, and risk-adjusted returns complete the picture. Interpreted over adequate samples and paired with process metrics to attribute results to skill, system, or variance.
concept.formula: Expectancy E = p_w * W_avg - p_l * L_avg, where p_w = win rate, W_avg = average win, p_l = loss rate, L_avg = average loss (in R-multiples or currency).
concept.failure_modes: Short-horizon outcome metrics are dominated by variance: dozens to hundreds of trades may be needed before expectancy estimates stabilize. Maximizing outcome metrics directly invites overfitting, hidden tail risk, and outcome-biased self-assessment.
concept.misconceptions: A profitable month does not prove a process improvement, and a losing month does not disprove one - sample size governs what outcome metrics can say. A high win rate alone is meaningless without the sizes of wins and losses.
concept.example: Over 200 journaled trades a system shows a 42% win rate, average win 2.3R, average loss 1.0R - expectancy about +0.39R per trade, a positive edge invisible in any single week.

citations.source: Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade: Inside the Highly Competitive World of Proprietary Trading (Wiley, 2010) - publisher page
